question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund's offshore sister-vehicle (a Mauritius feeder) appoints an on-site investment advisor in India. The principal purpose of the Investment Advisory Agreement in this context is:

answer.text: To transfer investment management powers entirely to the Indian advisor.
To set out the terms under which the Indian advisor renders ADVICE (deal assessment, execution, post-investment management) to the offshore manager.
To appoint the Indian advisor as the Trustee of the offshore fund.
To make the Indian advisor liable for FATCA reporting of all offshore investors.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 9.7.4 states: 'The Investment Advisory Agreement contains the general terms under which such investment advisor renders advisory functions.' The offshore manager retains ultimate responsibility to offshore investors, while the on-site advisor provides advice on deal assessment, execution and post-investment management. **The Trap:** Option A wrongly conflates advice with management. Option C confuses roles. Option D invents a tax-reporting flip that the advisory agreement does not confer. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the offshore-advisor arrangement across tracks. Section 9A of the IT Act (fund-management safe harbour) interplays with this structure — covered in XIX-E tax module. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Qualify the Indian advisor as a Section 9A-eligible 'eligible fund manager' to neutralise the offshore fund's business-connection / PE-India risk — this is a core reason unified Cat III macro / multi-strat funds route through the Indian advisor model.
